## What I changed

I agreed with the finding — the ~20-line Luhn algorithm inlined in the MapStruct interface broke the mapper's clear two-tier convention (trivial formatting inline; algorithmic derivations delegated to a `model`-package helper, as with `OwnerIdentity.of` and `CityRegions.localityOf`).

- **New `model/LuhnCheckDigit.java`** — a focused domain helper (`LuhnCheckDigit.of(String)`) holding the algorithm, with class-level javadoc explaining why it lives beside `Owner`, matching the style of its siblings. Returns `null` for a null input.
- **`OwnerMapper.toCheckDigit`** reduced to a one-line delegation: `return LuhnCheckDigit.of(owner.getCustomerCode());`, keeping the existing javadoc and matching `toIdentityKey`/`toLocality`.

On the reviewer's two extraction options, I took the `LuhnCheckDigit.of(String)` utility rather than introducing a full `CustomerCode` domain type and moving the format logic out of `AssignCustomerCode`. The check digit is a general-purpose numeric algorithm that's conceptually independent of the customer-code *format*, so a dedicated Luhn helper is the more cohesive home; folding a full `CustomerCode` refactor (relocating the `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>` format rules) into this change would be broader restructuring than the finding requires and would touch the create pipeline. This satisfies the core asks — algorithm out of the mapper, independently unit-testable, mapper thin and consistent — while keeping the change scoped.

The acceptance behaviour is unchanged (the algorithm is byte-for-byte identical), and the full suite passes.
